[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#scope]

## Scope

- If `$ARGUMENTS` is a PR number or URL, this Skill does not fetch that PR's diff or comments itself — it has no `execute`/GitHub-API tool. PR-number invocation routes through `/pr-appr-resolve`, which fetches the full diff and open review comments first and then invokes this Skill's Phase 0–4 judgment with that diff and those comments already supplied; the PR number/URL is used only for scoping and reporting context, never as a fetch trigger
- If `$ARGUMENTS` specifies a file path or pattern, scope the occurrence inventory to that file and its cross-file propagation partners
- Otherwise, operate on all uncommitted changes in the current working tree; if the working tree is clean (all changes already committed), operate on commits not yet pushed to the remote branch

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#when-to-invoke]

### When to Invoke

Invoke before committing or submitting for review whenever:

- You changed code that implements a concept described in standards, patterns, or cross-referenced documentation
- You changed how a concept is described in a standard or pattern (field lists, requirements, conditions, exceptions, classifications)
- You added or removed a conditional or exception to a requirement
- You changed a value that appears in multiple sections of the same document (description, components table, interactions, implementation steps, examples, TL;DR)
- Your change to one file logically implies a change to another file that references the same concept
- You renamed, moved, or changed the identity of a construct (a Skill, Agent, Command/Prompt, or file-pattern Instruction) — a rename always has logical parallels (every cross-reference to the old name) even when the rename itself is a single line
- You are processing review comments on an open PR — invoke `/pr-appr-resolve`, which applies this Skill's judgment as a **comprehensive pass across all open comments at once**, before making any edit

**Do not invoke for trivial single-line fixes** (typos, broken links, metadata field corrections) where the change has no logical parallel in any other section. **A rename or identity change never qualifies for this exclusion** — by definition it has parallel references elsewhere in the repo, regardless of how small the edit that introduced it looked.

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#coverage]

### Coverage

This Skill covers: occurrence inventory across changed files, cross-file propagation gaps, triage of open PR review comments (live/stale/deferred), pre-commit convergence verification, and detection of parallel statement gaps, prose-to-structure gaps, normative-authority mismatches, inter-document optionality contradictions, counter-to-enumeration mismatches, statement self-contradictions, claim-vs-instruction gaps, and incomplete fix substitutions.

This Skill does NOT cover: design decisions about what the correct content should be — delegate to `/documenter` for prose and documentation choices, or to `/architect` for architectural and structural decisions; fetching PR review threads, posting replies, resolving GitHub threads, or applying file edits — these operational steps belong to the invoking Command (`/eap-git`, `/eap-push`, or `/pr-appr-resolve` during an active PR review cycle), which consumes this Skill's judgment and performs them; committing changes after the convergence check passes (delegate to `/eap-git`).

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#skill-collaboration]

### Skill Collaboration

| Collaborator | Relationship |
|---|---|
| `documenter` | Runs before this Skill; may be re-invoked for delegated documentation fixes after convergence surfaces gaps — each re-invocation is followed by another convergence pass |
| `architect` | Receives design decisions revealed by convergence gaps |
| `eap-git` | Invokes this Skill's Phases 1–4 judgment as a pre-commit gate and performs the resulting file edits itself; Phase 4 must return pass before `eap-git` stages or commits |
| `eap-push` | Invokes this Skill's Phases 1–4 judgment as a pre-push gate before every push — both when auto-committing uncommitted changes and when the working tree is already clean with unpushed commits; performs the resulting file edits itself; does not push until this Skill's Phase 4 returns pass |
| `pr-appr-resolve` | Operational Command for an active PR review cycle — fetches open review comments and threads via `gh api`, applies this Skill's full Phase 0–4 judgment (comment triage, occurrence inventory, cross-file propagation, gap resolution, final checklist) to decide and draft each fix, then performs the file edits, replies, and thread-resolution mutations itself before handing off to `/eap-git`/`/eap-push` |

Position in the pipeline:

```text
/documenter → changes made → /ai-convergence → gaps found and resolved → /eap-git
/architect  → changes made → /ai-convergence → gaps found and resolved → /eap-git

Active PR review cycle:
review comments arrive → /pr-appr-resolve (applies this Skill's judgment across all open comments, one pass) → all gaps resolved → /eap-git → push once
```

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#the-core-problem-this-skill-addresses]

## The Core Problem This Skill Addresses

You have context. The reviewing AI does not.

You know you added field X to standard S and intended to update all patterns. You fixed occurrences in locations A, B, and C. But the reviewing AI reads location D cold and flags it because it only sees the diff and the full file — it has no memory of your intent.

The convergence problem is not about quality of changes. It's about **the gap between what you changed and what you verified**. The reviewing AI verifies the entire changed surface; you tend to verify only what you touched.

A second convergence problem occurs during active review cycles: **each push triggers a full re-review with no memory of prior rounds**. The reviewing AI re-reads the entire diff, escalates findings it deprioritized before, and finds new issues on recently changed lines. Fixing one comment per push guarantees the loop never closes.

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#the-cold-read-simulation]

## The Cold-Read Simulation

Before invoking, establish what the reviewing AI will see:

```text
Reviewing AI context:
- Sees the full diff (all changed files, all changed lines)
- Reads each changed file completely — not just the diff lines
- Has no memory of your intent, your prior rounds, or what you "meant" to fix
- Compares every statement against every other related statement in the same file
- Cross-references claims in patterns against the standards they cite
- Re-evaluates every prior finding on every push — previously deprioritized issues get escalated
```

The reviewing AI finds issues by pattern-matching. The patterns it reliably catches:

| Pattern | What it looks like | What gets flagged |
|---|---|---|
| **Parallel statement gap** | Concept X is described in N places in a file; you updated K < N | The K+1 through N occurrences still use the old description |
| **Prose-to-structure gap** | You updated descriptive prose to add a condition or exception; structured elements (diagrams, tables, step lists) still show the old unconditional behavior | The structured element contradicts the updated prose |
| **Cross-file propagation gap** | You added/changed a field or requirement in file A; other files in the diff enumerate that same field or requirement | Files B, C still use the old, shorter list |
| **Normative-authority mismatch** | A Standard, Pattern, Architecture Guidance, ADR, or Best Practice presents a `MUST`/`SHALL` requirement as already binding or enforceable while its own status or the status of every cited authority is `draft`, `proposed`, or otherwise not ratified — a draft proposing Mandatory Requirements is normal and not itself a defect | The claim of current enforceability is flagged as unsupported by an established mandate. Skills and Commands are behavioral guidelines and are not subject to this check. |
| **Inter-document optionality contradiction** | Document A calls behavior X mandatory; a companion document in the same diff describes the same behavior X as optional or skippable | One document contradicts the other; readers cannot know which governs |
| **Counter-to-enumeration mismatch** | A heading, intro, or summary states a count (e.g., "12 core skills," "5 phases"); the actual enumeration has a different number of items | The stated count does not match the real item count — a mechanical discrepancy the AI catches by counting |
| **Statement self-contradiction** | A single row, bullet, or sentence encodes two mutually exclusive temporal states or logical claims (e.g., "runs before X; implements fixes identified by X") | The statement is internally incoherent — a reader cannot satisfy both claims simultaneously |
| **Claim-vs-instruction gap** | A document explicitly states a coverage goal, risk mitigation, or outcome — often as a warning (e.g., "a repo with zero commits on the default branch is easy to miss") — but its own procedure does not deliver that claim; the steps still produce the gap the document warns about | The document promises X while its instructions produce Y — the stated goal and the actual steps are decoupled |
| **Duplicate structured entry** | A concept should have exactly one row or bullet in a table, list, or diagram; a fix adds a new entry for that concept without first checking whether one already exists | Two rows for the same collaborator, tool, or concept in the same structure — a reader cannot determine which is authoritative |

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#phase-0-triage-open-comments]

### Phase 0: Triage Open Comments

Before building any occurrence inventory, determine which comments are still live. This phase supplies classification judgment only — fetching the comments and resolving threads on GitHub are operational steps performed by the invoking Command (`/pr-appr-resolve`), not by this Skill.

In a multi-round PR, each push triggers a full re-review with no memory of prior rounds. Previously-fixed content gets re-raised alongside genuinely new issues — the noise is indistinguishable from signal until you read the current file state.

For each open review comment the invoking Command supplies:

1. Identify the file and location the comment targets
2. Read the current file state at that location
3. Classify the comment:

| Status | Condition | Action |
|---|---|---|
| **Live** | The issue is still present in the current file | Add to the occurrence inventory in Phase 1 |
| **Stale** | The issue no longer exists in the current file | No edit; classify for resolution and skip Phase 1 for this comment |
| **Deferred** | The issue is real but intentionally not fixed in this PR | Record the deferral explicitly (see Phase 3); skip Phase 1 |
| **False Positive** | The comment makes a mechanically verifiable claim (path depth, field count, list length, link resolution) that is independently confirmed incorrect | No edit; classify as a false positive using the same path as Stale (see The False Fix anti-pattern); skip Phase 1 |

Do not build an occurrence inventory for a stale comment. Do not edit a file in response to a comment if the current file already satisfies it — re-editing correct content to match a stale comment re-introduces a gap.

**A classification is not complete until the invoking Command actually resolves the thread on GitHub.** GitHub does not reliably auto-detect that a later, unrelated commit already satisfied an earlier comment — the thread's `isOutdated` flag can remain `false` indefinitely even when the content is fixed. An open, unresolved thread is indistinguishable from a genuinely new issue on the next triage pass, so this Skill requires `/pr-appr-resolve` to resolve every Stale or False Positive thread immediately after classification, in the same pass — never batched for "later," and never left unconfirmed.

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#phase-1-map-the-change-surface]

### Phase 1: Map the Change Surface

For each file you changed:

1. **Read the entire file** — not just the lines you edited. Every section.

   While reading, run a **pre-existing inconsistency scan**: for every concept in the file that has both a prose description AND a structured representation (diagram node, table cell, step list item), check whether they agree — even for concepts you did not change. Automated peer reviewers (Copilot, second-AI reviewers) read the whole file on every push and will flag a pre-existing diagram/prose mismatch in a file you touched, even if your diff didn't touch that section. (The project `/ea-reviewer` skill is intentionally diff-scoped; this scan addresses automated reviewer behavior.) When you touch a file, you adopt responsibility for its full internal state.

2. **Identify the concept changed** — state it in one sentence: "I changed [what] in [which standard/pattern] to [the new value/condition]."
3. **Find all parallel occurrences** — search the file for every other place that concept appears:
   - Descriptions, overviews, solution summaries
   - Components tables, interactions lists, step-by-step sequences
   - Diagrams (Mermaid or otherwise) — every node and edge label
   - Variations and edge cases
   - Use case examples and scenarios
   - Before/after comparisons
   - TL;DR sections, key benefits, key rules

   **Search all morphological variants.** If the concept is a verb or noun with multiple forms (e.g., `register` → `registered`, `registering`, `registration`), search for each form separately. Searching only the exact phrase you changed will miss inflected occurrences that carry the same meaning and will be flagged as contradictions by the reviewing AI.

4. **Build an occurrence inventory:**

   ```text
   Concept: [what changed]
   File: [filename]

   | # | Section | Type | Current text (excerpt) | Status |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | 1 | Solution Overview | prose | "...unconditional statement..." | ✓ updated |
   | 2 | Architecture Diagram | Mermaid node | "Execute Write or Action" | ❌ missing branch |
   | 3 | Components Table | table cell | "Presents all Write/Action..." | ❌ not qualified |
   | 4 | Interactions step 4 | numbered list | "agent presents to user..." | ❌ not qualified |
   | 5 | Phase 3 step 2 | numbered list | "for each Write or Action..." | ✓ updated |
   | 6 | Compliance Requirements | bullet | "Human checkpoint required..." | ❌ not qualified |
   | 7 | TL;DR Key Benefits | bullet | "...explicit human confirmation" | ✓ updated |
   ```

5. **Repeat across all changed files.** For each file, build its occurrence inventory.

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#phase-2-map-cross-file-propagation]

### Phase 2: Map Cross-File Propagation

> **Scope in an active PR review cycle:** "changed files" means every file in the PR diff across all commits — not just files you are editing in the current session. Touching any file in the diff triggers a full re-read of the entire diff by the reviewing AI. A file you haven't touched since push 1 will be re-reviewed on push 10. When building the cross-file map, search across the entire PR diff, not just files with open comments or files in the current edit session.

For each concept changed in any file, identify all other changed files that reference the same concept:

```text
Concept: System Connection Register field list
Changed in: STD-TEC-AI-008 (authoritative definition)

Other changed files that enumerate SCR fields:
- PTN-TEC-AI-007: Solution step 1 ✓, Components table ✓, Interactions step 1 ❌
- PTN-TEC-AI-009: Solution step 5 ✓, Interactions step 5 ❌, Phase 1 step 6 ✓
- PTN-GOV-AI-010: Component 6 description ✓
```

A cross-file propagation is complete only when **every enumeration in every changed file matches the authoritative source**.

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#phase-2a-removal-propagation-when-diff-contains-deletions]

### Phase 2a: Removal Propagation (when diff contains deletions)

**Trigger**: The diff includes one or more deleted files — skill directories (`.claude/skills/<name>/`), command files (`.claude/commands/<name>.md`), prompt files (`.github/prompts/<name>.prompt.md`), or any other named construct invoked by prose reference.

**Scope**: Unlike Phase 2, this sub-phase searches the **entire repository** — not just changed files. The reviewing AI will flag orphaned references in files nowhere near the diff. This sub-phase is the ai-convergence equivalent of the ea-reviewer's "orphan risk on removals" check (ea-reviewer/SKILL.md).

**Steps**:

1. **Collect all removed names** — for each deleted skill, command, or prompt, extract the canonical invocation name (e.g., `coder` from `.claude/skills/coder/`; `eap-lint` from `.claude/commands/eap-lint.md`).

2. **Search the entire repo** for each removed name using construct-specific patterns — a skill-shaped pattern will not find a dangling Command or Prompt reference:
   - **Skills** — backtick-quoted invocations (`` `/coder` ``), bold references (`**coder**`), prose (`the coder skill`, `delegate to coder`), file paths (`.claude/skills/coder/SKILL.md`, `.github/skills/coder/`)
   - **Commands** — slash invocations (`` `/eap-lint` ``), file paths (`.claude/commands/eap-lint.md`), prose (`the eap-lint command`, `run eap-lint`)
   - **Prompts** — file paths (`.github/prompts/eap-lint.prompt.md`), prose references to the prompt mirror
   - Also check documentation that lists the construct as a worked example or reference-implementation catalog entry — these are exactly as orphaned as a direct invocation but easy to miss because they read as illustrative rather than functional

3. **Exclude false positives**:
   - Code variables, config keys, and role names that coincidentally share the skill name (e.g., a Python variable `optimizer =` is not a reference to the `optimizer` skill; a role `studio-deployer` is not the `deployer` skill). Use surrounding context to distinguish genuine skill references from coincidental matches.
   - A removed Skill/Command/Prompt name is not an orphaned local reference when the referencing document explicitly documents that construct as hosted in a **different, named repository** — e.g., a table or prose stating "this command is owned by eap-bootstrap" — rather than this repo's own `.claude/`/`.github/` catalog. This repo already contains exactly this pattern: [GUID-TECH-IMPL-006](../../../strategy/guidance/technology/implementation/GUID-TECH-IMPL-006-claude-code-command-authoring-guidance.md) has a Naming Conventions table explicitly mapping `eap-` prefixed commands to the `eap-bootstrap` repository as their owner. A search hit against that pattern (or any equivalent explicit cross-repo attribution) is not flagged as an orphaned local reference.

4. **Add every genuine hit to the occurrence inventory** for Phase 3. Each hit is an orphaned reference that must be updated or removed before the PR can merge cleanly.

5. **Treat the first hit in a file as a trigger for a full-file scan, not the fix.** When step 2 finds a genuine hit in a file, that file has adopted the removed construct as an internal concept — apply Phase 1's occurrence inventory to the removed name across that **entire file** before editing anything, the same as any other changed concept. Fixing only the specific line the search matched and moving to the next file is The Flagged-Line-Only Fix applied to Phase 2a specifically; a file that references a deleted construct once frequently references it five or ten more times as a naming example, a decision-tree branch, a reference-implementation catalog row, or a delegation target.

**Skip this sub-phase when the diff contains no file deletions.**

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#phase-2b-pointermirror-consistency-when-diff-touches-a-skill-or-command-file]

### Phase 2b: Pointer/Mirror Consistency (when diff touches a Skill or Command file)

**Trigger**: The diff modifies, adds, or renames a `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` file or a `.claude/commands/<name>.md` file. Unlike Phase 2a, this phase does not require a deletion — a file that still exists but was renamed, or whose content changed, can still leave its Copilot mirror stale.

**Why this is not just a Phase 2a case**: Phase 2a's search patterns are keyed to a fully removed construct name. A stale mirror left over from a rename or prefix change (e.g., `git.md` → `eap-git.md`) leaves the underlying construct alive under a new canonical name, so a removed-name search will not surface it — the mirror still resolves to a real file, it just resolves to the wrong one.

**Steps**:

1. For each changed `.claude/commands/<name>.md`, locate its paired `.github/prompts/<name>.prompt.md` (if one exists) and verify the mirror's canonical-path reference resolves to the current `.claude/commands/<name>.md` filename — not a prior or pre-rename one.
2. For each changed `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, locate its paired `.github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` pointer (if one exists) and verify its frontmatter `name`/`description` are consistent with the canonical Skill. `ea-reviewer/SKILL.md` scopes to the `foundation/CONTRIBUTING.md` EA artifact taxonomy and does not check Skill, Agent, or Command files — this Phase is the *only* place pointer/mirror consistency for AI constructs is verified; do not assume the reviewing AI will catch a stale pointer.
3. If no mirror exists for a changed Command or Skill, that is a gap requiring parity under [STD-TEC-AI-004](../../../standards/technology/ai-development/STD-TEC-AI-004-workflow-authoring.md) MR-1.5 (every Workflow present in one platform format MUST have a corresponding Workflow in the other) — add it to the occurrence inventory for Phase 3 resolution. The only recognized narrowing is STD-TEC-AI-004's own Exceptions Process: an approved exception recorded as a comment at the top of the Workflow file, documenting the specific requirement excepted (MR-1.5) and the rationale. Confirm silently and move on only when that recorded comment is present in the file; otherwise the missing mirror is a defect, not a silent pass.

**Skip this sub-phase when the diff touches no Skill or Command file.**

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#phase-3-resolve-all-gaps]

### Phase 3: Resolve All Gaps

For every ❌ in your occurrence inventories:

1. **Before inserting any new row, bullet, or entry into a structured element** (table, numbered list, diagram), read the entire element first. If an entry for the same concept already exists, update or merge it — do not add. Every concept has exactly one representation per structured element. An additive fix to a structured element is always wrong when an entry for that concept is already present.
2. Determine the precise edit needed to reflect the change — the invoking Command applies it to the file
3. After the edit is applied, verify it does not create a new ❌ elsewhere in the same file (a new phrase may introduce a new parallel that also needs updating)
4. Mark it ✓

For any gap you are **deliberately not fixing in this PR** (out of scope, pending a separate decision, tracked elsewhere):

4. Record the deferral explicitly — a note in the PR description, a resolution comment on the open review comment, or a linked follow-up issue. Do not leave it silently unaddressed. An unresolved comment with no deferral record will be re-raised by the reviewing AI on every subsequent push.

Do not commit until all occurrence inventories show only ✓ or explicitly-recorded deferrals.

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#phase-4-run-the-convergence-check]

### Phase 4: Run the Convergence Check

Before committing, run the following verification pass mentally or explicitly:

**For each changed file:**
- [ ] Every diagram matches the text in the same section
- [ ] Every table cell that describes a concept matches the prose description of the same concept
- [ ] Every numbered step list covers the same cases as the surrounding prose
- [ ] No section uses the old, unqualified version of a concept that was qualified elsewhere in the same file
- [ ] For every heading renamed, verify no `#anchor` reference in the document still uses the old slug
- [ ] For every section heading, verify the heading still accurately describes its section body after any conditional qualifications were added to that body — a heading like "Registration" that describes an unconditional action becomes stale when conditional language makes it apply only to some cases
- [ ] For any section that declares its children mutually exclusive ("choose one"), verify no child's body prose qualifies or overrides that framing
- [ ] For each normative citation, verify the cited document's declared scope covers the scenario this document claims it governs
- [ ] For each item in a scope, applicability, or "this guidance covers" list, verify a corresponding section or procedure exists that fulfills it
- [ ] For any instruction to unset, remove, or delete a setting or file, identify all other tools or workflows that depend on it and confirm removal is safe for each
- [ ] For any configuration block, flag when the same logical setting appears in more than one form — either remove the redundancy or explicitly explain which takes precedence
- [ ] For every table, numbered list, or structured element where a new row or entry was added in this pass: verify no other entry in the same structure covers the same concept. A table with two rows for the same collaborator, tool, or item is always a defect regardless of whether each row is individually correct
- [ ] For every `MUST`, `SHALL`, or normative statement **in a Standard, Pattern, Architecture Guidance, ADR, or Best Practice** (not Skills or Commands — those are behavioral guidelines): verify the statement is not presented as already binding or enforceable while the document's own status is `draft`/`proposed`, or while it depends entirely on a cited authority that is itself `draft`/`proposed`. A `draft` artifact is expected to propose Mandatory Requirements — that is the normal drafting lifecycle, not a defect. The real defect is language asserting current enforceability (e.g., "teams must comply with this today") for a requirement that has not yet cleared governance ratification — recast that language as proposed/pending ratification, or establish and cite a ratified authority first
- [ ] For every behavior described as mandatory in this file: verify no companion document in the diff describes the same behavior as optional (or vice versa). If one document calls a gate required and another calls it optional, the contradiction will be flagged regardless of which is correct
- [ ] For any heading, section intro, or summary that states a count (e.g., "12 core skills", "5 phases", "three required fields"): verify the count matches the actual number of items in the enumeration it describes. Recount; do not rely on memory of what the count was before you edited
- [ ] For each table row, bullet, or sentence that describes a relationship or sequence: verify the statement is internally logically coherent — a description like "runs before X; implements fixes identified by X" is self-contradictory because implementing fixes X identifies requires running after X, not before it. When a single statement encodes two mutually exclusive temporal states or conditions, split it or reframe to resolve the contradiction
- [ ] For any statement where the document acknowledges a risk or coverage limitation and then claims to address it (e.g., "X is easy to miss — so we do Y"): verify the steps that follow actually close the gap. A warning paired with steps that still produce the warned-about gap is a claim-vs-instruction mismatch
- [ ] For any fix in this pass that substitutes one tool, method, or approach for another: verify the replacement does not carry the same limitation as the original. Confirm independently that the substitution resolves the specific constraint — "it's a different call" is not evidence the problem is solved. If the replacement requires additional configuration to avoid the same limitation, document that configuration explicitly rather than leaving it implied
- [ ] No convergence fix in this pass expands the scope, adds new capabilities, changes the design intent, or shifts the audience of the artifact — each edit aligns existing statements to what the artifact already means to say. If closing a gap requires changing what the artifact does, that is a design decision; surface it to `/architect` or `/documenter` instead of applying it here

**Across all changed files** (in a PR review cycle: all files in the PR diff, not just files edited in this session)**:**
- [ ] Every enumeration of concept X lists the same items, in every file that enumerates X
- [ ] No file still says "all Y must Z" when another changed file now says "all Y except approved-A must Z"
- [ ] Every open review comment is either resolved (the underlying issue is fixed in this pass) or explicitly deferred with a recorded note. No comment should be silently skipped
- [ ] For any Skill or Command file changed in this diff, verify its paired Copilot mirror (`.github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` or `.github/prompts/<name>.prompt.md`) references it by current filename, not a prior or renamed one

If any check fails, return to Phase 3.

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#the-one-comment-per-push-fix]

### The One-Comment-Per-Push Fix

```text
WRONG: Review comment arrives. You fix that one comment, push.
       Three new comments arrive on the next review round.
       You fix those, push. Four more arrive. The loop never closes.
```

Fix approach: When processing review comments on an open PR, **treat all open comments as a single batch**. Invoke `/pr-appr-resolve`, which applies this Skill's judgment as a comprehensive pass across every open comment simultaneously. The reviewing AI re-reads the entire diff with no memory of prior rounds — every push is a full re-review. Fix everything in one edit session, push once.

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#the-flagged-line-only-fix]

### The Flagged-Line-Only Fix

```text
WRONG: Copilot flags line 97. You read line 97, fix line 97, commit.
       Lines 42, 118, 203, and 315 describe the same concept. Not checked.
```

Fix approach: When a review comment points to a line, treat it as a **symptom** pointing to a concept. Find all occurrences of that concept in the file, not just the flagged line.

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#the-prose-without-structure-fix]

### The Prose-Without-Structure Fix

```text
WRONG: You add "unless autonomous execution is approved" to the solution description.
       The architecture diagram still shows all Write/Action going to human confirmation.
       The components table still says "presents all Write/Action to user."
       The interactions section still says "agent presents to user."
```

Fix approach: Every prose change that introduces a condition or exception must be reflected in every structured element (diagram, table, numbered list) in the same document.

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#the-partial-cross-file-fix]

### The Partial Cross-File Fix

```text
WRONG: Standard gains field F. You update 3 patterns to include F.
       A 4th pattern in the diff also enumerates the same fields. Not checked.
```

Fix approach: When updating a field list, search all changed files for the concept name. If a file appears in the diff and contains an enumeration of those fields, it is in scope regardless of whether a review comment pointed to it.

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#the-i-already-fixed-that-assumption]

### The "I Already Fixed That" Assumption

```text
WRONG: "I fixed the human confirmation statement in this file already."
       You fixed it in the Solution section. The Interactions section, diagram,
       components table, and Compliance Requirements section were not checked.
```

Fix approach: "Already fixed" applies only to the specific occurrence you fixed, not to the concept. The concept must be verified at every occurrence, not declared complete after one fix.

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#the-silent-deferral]

### The Silent Deferral

```text
WRONG: Review comment points to a real issue you've decided not to fix in this PR.
       You make no note of it. The reviewing AI re-raises it on the next push.
       And the next. And the next.
```

Fix approach: A deliberate deferral is a decision, not an oversight. Record it — resolve the review comment with an explanation, add a PR description note, or link a follow-up issue. The reviewing AI cannot distinguish "decided not to fix" from "missed" — only explicit recording stops the re-raise.
page_texts.23:
[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#the-premature-commit]

### The Premature Commit

```text
WRONG: You complete the intended edits. The changes look right to you.
       You run git add and commit before completing Phase 4.
       You find additional gaps only after the commit exists —
       now you need follow-up commits to fix what Phase 4 would have caught.
```

Fix approach: **Phase 4 is a hard gate before staging, committing, or pushing.** "Intended edits complete" is not the same as "Phase 4 complete." Do not stage or commit until every Phase 4 checklist item has been verified for every changed file. Finding gaps after committing means Phase 4 was skipped, not deferred.

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#the-accidental-adopter]

### The Accidental Adopter

```text
WRONG: You touch a file to fix one thing — a step list, a cross-reference, a condition.
       The file had a pre-existing mismatch on a different concept: a diagram that
       contradicts the prose, a table cell that omits a requirement the standard already
       mandates. You didn't introduce it. But on the next push, Copilot reads the whole
       file and flags it anyway. You're blamed for a gap you inherited.
```

Fix approach: **When you touch a file, you adopt responsibility for its entire internal state.** Automated peer reviewers (Copilot, second-AI reviewers) read the entire changed file — not only the diff lines — and do not distinguish "your diff" from "pre-existing content." (The project `/ea-reviewer` skill is intentionally scoped to the diff only; this anti-pattern describes automated tool behavior.) Do the pre-existing inconsistency scan in Phase 1 step 1 — for every concept in the file with both prose and structured representations, check whether they agree, even for concepts you didn't change. A file that was inconsistent before you touched it is consistently inconsistent after you leave it.

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#the-incomplete-fix-substitution]

### The Incomplete Fix Substitution

```text
WRONG: A review comment flags that tool A has limitation L (e.g., only
       searches the default branch). You substitute tool B as a fix.
       Tool B has the same limitation L by default — it just has a
       different name. The gap is renamed, not resolved.
```

Fix approach: When a fix substitutes one tool, method, or approach for another, verify the replacement does not carry the same limitation. Independently confirm that the replacement lacks the specific constraint that made the original deficient — "it's a different call" is not the same as "it solves the problem." If the replacement requires additional configuration to avoid the same limitation, document that configuration explicitly rather than leaving it implied.

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#the-additive-fix]

### The Additive Fix

```text
WRONG: A collaboration table has a row for eap-push.
       You need to replace an eap-finalize row with one describing eap-push.
       Without reading the whole table first, you add a new eap-push row.
       The table now has two rows for eap-push — one from before, one from the fix.
```

Fix approach: Before adding any new row, bullet, or entry to a structured element, **read the entire element**. If an entry for the same concept already exists, update or merge it — never add alongside. Structured elements (tables, lists, diagrams) have one entry per concept. The reviewing AI will spot the duplicate immediately; the fix takes longer to explain than it would have taken to check.

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#the-false-fix]

### The False Fix

```text
WRONG: A review comment asserts that a path is one level too deep,
       a field count is wrong, or a link resolves incorrectly.
       You accept the claim, edit the file to match, and push.
       The edit introduces a real defect — the original was correct.
```

Fix approach: For any comment that makes a structural or mechanical claim — path depth, field count, list length, link resolution, reference numbering — verify the claim independently before editing. Do not rely solely on the reviewer's assertion.

Verification methods for mechanical claims:
- **Path depth**: Count `../` segments and trace the resolved path manually from the file's directory
- **Field count / list length**: Count the items in the authoritative source, then count the items in the flagged location — the discrepancy either confirms or refutes the comment
- **Control file test**: Find a neighboring file in the same directory that uses the same pattern and is not flagged. If it exists and the pattern is consistent, the comment is likely a false positive — both files should behave the same under the same rule

A review comment that is factually wrong does not become correct by receiving no response. Record it as a false positive using the same path as a stale comment — no edit, but an explicit note if the comment is open and visible. Editing correct content to satisfy an incorrect mechanical claim creates a defect that the next reviewer will flag as a regression.

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#ownership]

### Ownership

- This Skill owns: convergence verification findings, occurrence inventories, gap assessments, deferral records, and the classification criteria distinguishing an unambiguous fix from a design decision
- This Skill does not itself modify files or call GitHub APIs — the invoking Command (`/eap-git`, `/eap-push`, `/pr-appr-resolve`) applies the resulting file edits, delegating design decisions to `/documenter` or `/architect`
page_texts.30:
[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#delegation]

### Delegation

- This Skill determines when a fix is unambiguous — e.g., updating a count that doesn't match its enumeration, aligning a duplicate statement, correcting a cross-reference — versus when it requires a design decision; the invoking Command performs the actual file edit either way
- Delegate to `/documenter` when a gap requires choosing between competing prose descriptions or deciding what the correct content should be in documentation artifacts
- Delegate to `/architect` when a gap reveals an architectural or structural ambiguity — architecture and design authority routes here
- This Skill does not invoke `/eap-git`, `/eap-push`, or `/pr-appr-resolve` itself — per `STD-TEC-AI-001`:156 and `PTN-TEC-AI-004`:143-164, Commands orchestrate and consume Skills, not the reverse. Instead, `/eap-git` and `/eap-push` invoke this Skill's Phases 1–4 judgment as a gate before committing or pushing, and `/pr-appr-resolve` invokes this Skill's full Phase 0–4 judgment during an active PR review cycle — fetching comments, applying file edits, and resolving GitHub threads itself; each proceeds only when Phase 4 returns pass

[.claude/skills/ai-convergence/SKILL.md#constraints]

### Constraints

- This Skill owns the judgment for identifying **unambiguous fixes** (aligning what a document says with what it already means to say) and the **verification pass**; the invoking Command performs the actual edit. It does not own design decisions — if a gap reveals an ambiguity about what the correct content should be, surface it to `/architect` or `/documenter` before resolving.
- The occurrence inventory is not optional. The patchwork behavior this Skill prevents is caused by skipping the inventory and trusting memory.
- A concept is considered consistent when every occurrence in every changed file reflects the same state. Partial consistency is not consistency.
- Diagrams are structured elements. A prose change that is not reflected in the diagram is not complete.
- Cross-file propagation is not complete until the authoritative source and every referencing file in the diff agree on every field, condition, and classification.
- **Fixes must preserve the existing scope and design intent of the artifact.** A convergence fix aligns what a document says with what it already means to say — it does not add new capabilities, expand coverage claims, change the artifact's audience, or alter its design decisions. If closing a gap requires a scope change (the only correct fix is to change what the document does), that is a design decision — surface it to `/architect` or `/documenter` rather than applying it as a convergence fix.
- When in an active PR review cycle, this Skill is the gate before **every push**, not just the first. Run it after receiving any batch of review comments and before making the first edit.
- In an active PR review cycle, "all changed files" in Phases 1–4 means the **entire PR diff**, not the current session's edits. Phase 2 cross-file propagation must search the whole diff. Scoping the search to only files you are currently editing is the most common source of new findings on the next push — the reviewing AI has no such scope limit.
- "Deferred" is not the same as "ignored." A review comment you decide not to address in this PR must be explicitly recorded as deferred. Silence reads as oversight to the reviewing AI — it will re-raise the comment on every subsequent push until the code changes or the deferral is recorded.
